title: Revelations of Divine Love
author: Julian of Norwich (Warrack ed)
description: Revelations of Divine Love by Julian of Norwich (c. 1342-after 1416), edited by Grace Warrack from the British Museum Sloane manuscript (Methuen, 1901), the edition that made Julian widely known. An anchoress at St Julian's Church in Norwich, she received sixteen 'shewings' during a severe illness in May 1373 and spent twenty years reflecting on them, producing the earliest surviving book in English known to be written by a woman. The visions centre on Christ's Passion and reveal the overwhelming love of God. Themes include the hazelnut as an image of all creation held in being by love, the parable of the lord and the servant reinterpreting the Fall, sin as 'behovely', the motherhood of God and Christ, and the assurance that 'all shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well'. Warrack supplies an introduction and glossary. It is one of the most beloved works of Christian mysticism.
